text: Agile methodology is a popular approach to project management, especially in software development. Instead of tackling a huge project all at once, the work is broken down into short phases called sprints, which usually last two to four weeks. Each sprint focuses on delivering a small, usable piece of the product. A key part of this process is the backlog, a prioritized list of tasks and features that still need to be done. These tasks are often written as user stories, which describe a feature from the end-user’s perspective. Team members also hold daily standups—short meetings where everyone shares what they did yesterday, what they will do today, and any obstacles they face. This focus on iterative development allows teams to adapt quickly to change and gather feedback early, ensuring the final product truly meets the customer’s needs.
